headline: Scientific inquiry asks questions nature must answer—through observation and experiment
universal_truth: The universe doesn't lie; ask the right questions and observe carefully, and reality will teach you
fun_facts: The scientific method has only existed for about 400 years—before that, knowledge was often just authority
Science advances by falsification—proving old ideas wrong, not just confirming them
Peer review means scientists check each other's work before it's published
discussion_questions: How do you investigate questions when you don't know the answer?
What would a 'scientific approach' look like in your daily decisions?
How do you distinguish between what you've tested and what you've assumed?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Before science, we asked authorities. Now we ask nature directly—through observation and experiment. The universe doesn't lie, doesn't have opinions, doesn't play favorites. Ask the right questions, and reality will answer.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Science transformed our world by changing how we get knowledge. What's special about scientific inquiry?

options.text: Science forces reality to answer—it doesn't rely on authority, tradition, or intuition alone; it tests ideas against nature, and nature doesn't lie; wrong ideas get exposed
options.response: Yes. Science is humble before reality. Ideas must face evidence. Wrong ideas get corrected. It's a self-correcting system that converges on truth over time.
True, but the method—testing against reality—is what makes those facts reliable...

q1.title: Question Formulation
q1.script: Good science starts with good questions—specific enough to test, open enough to surprise. 'How does this work?' 'What would happen if?' The question frames the investigation.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Question Formulation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Controlled Testing
q2.script: Experiments control variables to isolate causes. Change one thing, keep others constant, observe what happens. This reveals causation, not just correlation.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Science
q3.script: You can apply scientific thinking personally: ask clear questions, make predictions, test against reality, update based on results. Reality will teach you—if you let it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The universe doesn't lie. Ask the right questions and observe carefully, and reality will teach you. Be a scientist of your own life.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 296. Tomorrow, we'll explore seeing on purpose—observation. Until then, formulate a question and let reality answer.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Personal Experiment - What Can Reality Teach You?
growTrack.learning_objective: Apply scientific inquiry to personal questions
growTrack.activity: Pick a question about your life you don't know the answer to. Formulate it clearly. What test or observation would give you an answer? Design a small experiment and let reality teach you.
